angle: token geometry of the quantizer input: fixed versus learned front end at matched reconstruction
study_sentence: A seed-paired training experiment in which the front end of one EEG tokenizer is assigned to a learned convolution, a frozen filter bank, the frozen filter bank with a fixed whitening, or the frozen filter bank with rank-matched noise, with codebook perplexity over steps 10,000-16,000 as the outcome, on sleep EEG (ISRUC, Sleep-EDF) and repeated on awake EEG (EEGBCI).
question: Why does a frozen filter-bank front end that reconstructs as well as a learned convolution give lower codebook perplexity in an EEG tokenizer: is the deficit set by the anisotropy of its tokens, which a fixed whitening removes without any training, or by the absence of a trained front end?

angle_parts.part: token geometry of the quantizer input

datasets: ISRUC-Sleep + Sleep-EDF telemetry (project h5, one preprocessing pipeline)
inventory: ~/mne_data/MNE-eegbci-data: 109 subjects, awake, other amplifier, no ASR needed - used as the second dataset in E6
~/mne_data/sleep-edf-s3: 20 raw Sleep-EDF cassette recordings, 2 EEG channels - would serve as a third pool, not used to keep the budget
~/mne_data: the other sets (lee2019, bnci, gigadb, braininvaders, epflp300, erpcore, liu2020beta, nakanishi, wang) are task BCI data - usable, add nothing over EEGBCI for this contrast
~/openneuro_data: ds003478, ds003775, ds003810, ds004148, ds004784, ds006801, ds007176, ds007222, ds007406, ds007558 - resting and task sets cached for an earlier topic; usable, not needed
/Users/kyc/PythonProject/LaBraM/data: ISRUC + Sleep-EDF telemetry pretraining h5 (the primary pool; one preprocessing pipeline)
/Users/kyc/PythonProject/LaBraM/checkpoints: trained tokenizers of the project record - reference numbers only, not evidence for the claim

claims.statement: Although the codebook perplexity deficit of a frozen filter-bank front end against a learned convolution is read as the price of not training it, a fixed whitening of its tokens closes at least half of that deficit, because the deficit is set by the anisotropy of the tokens the encoder receives.
reasons: Flattening the variance spectrum of the frozen front end's tokens, with no gradient reaching the front end, raises codebook perplexity by at least half of the gap to the learned convolution.
The gain is not produced by noise that merely raises the tokens' rank.

evidence.measure: codebook perplexity = exp(entropy of the quantizer's EMA code-usage shares), read every 200 steps -> mean over steps 10,000-16,000 per run -> per seed G = P_W - P_F and D = P_L - P_F -> mean over 5 seeds; validation loss per run at step 16,000
evidence.would_show: mean G >= 0.5 mean D with W's validation loss within 5% of F's
evidence.refuted_if: mean G < 0.5 * mean D over the 5 seeds, or validation loss of W more than 5% above F
evidence.can_fail: yes: the manipulation acts on the 256-dimensional token at the encoder's input, the measure is read at the codebook after 12 trained layers; the encoder may map raw and whitened tokens to the same z distribution, or whitening may lower usage

evidence.measure: same perplexity path for arm N (frozen bank + Gaussian noise matched to W's token effective rank), 3 seeds: mean of P_W - P_N and of P_N - P_F
evidence.would_show: P_W - P_N > 0 and P_N - P_F below 0.5 mean D
evidence.can_fail: yes: noise is added to the same tokens the encoder reads, so it can raise usage as much as whitening does

evidence.measure: the E2 path on EEGBCI (6 channels, 250 Hz), arms L, F, W, 2 seeds: mean G and mean D
evidence.would_show: the same sign and a closure of at least half
evidence.refuted_if: mean G < 0.5 * mean D on EEGBCI (2 seeds; reported as agreement or disagreement, no test)
evidence.can_fail: yes: same reasons as E2, on data with another spectrum and no corpus blocking

construction.predictor_formula: t'_i = s * C_shrunk^(-1/2) * (t_i - m), C_shrunk = 0.9*C + 0.1*(tr C / 256)*I, m and C from 20,000 training patches
construction.outcome_formula: P = exp(-sum_k p_k * ln p_k) averaged over steps 10,000-16,000, p_k = EMA usage share of code k; statistic G = P_W - P_F against 0.5*(P_L - P_F)
construction.computable_without_experiment: no: p_k is the share of patches whose normalised encoder output falls in code k's cell after 16,000 steps of joint training; existing data give neither the trained encoder under whitening nor its codebook (only the tokens' own effective rank follows from algebra, and it is not in the rule)
construction.free_quantity: how the jointly trained encoder and the EMA cosine codebook transmit the geometry of their input to code usage

claims.warrant: When an outcome follows a manipulation that changes only the second-order statistics of a fixed front end's output, with the front end untrained in both arms, then the outcome's difference between the arms is attributable to those statistics and not to learning in the front end.

outcomes.if_supported: we learn that an analytic front end needs a fixed normalisation stage, not gradients, to feed a discrete codebook, and that usage differences between tokenizers may reflect input geometry
outcomes.if_not: we learn that flattening the token spectrum is not enough, so training pressure on the front end (or something else it supplies) is necessary and the gradient starvation of structured front ends is the problem to solve

negation.text: A fixed whitening of the frozen front end's tokens closes less than half of the deficit.

expected_direction.basis: contested: zhaoetal2026 predicts a gain from flattening what is quantized; the project record's reading and andersonetal2023 (a non-moving front end is an optimisation failure) predict that training is what is missing

claims.falsifier: E2: mean over 5 seeds of G = P_W - P_F is below 0.5 times the mean of D = P_L - P_F, or the validation loss of W is more than 5% above that of F; read only if E1 shows mean D > 0 at one-sided paired p < 0.05

rivals.how: whitening amplifies low-variance token directions that carry noise, so codes spread over noise and perplexity rises without more usable codes
perplexity varies between runs and only 5 seeds are used
rivals.ruled_out_by: E2 (paired one-sided test and 90% CI over seeds)

rivals.how: the outcome window or probe schedule could be chosen after seeing the curves
rivals.ruled_out_by: design: window 10,000-16,000 and the 200-step probe fixed before any run

rivals.how: whitening changes the token scale and so the effective step size of the encoder
rivals.ruled_out_by: design: the scalar s matches the mean squared token norm of W to F

rivals.how: whitening statistics or the outcome computed on data the model was fit to
rivals.ruled_out_by: design: m and C from training patches only; perplexity also reported on validation patches

rivals.how: the bank configuration (48 poles, 8 oscillators) is the most anisotropic one in the project record, so the effect may not hold for other banks

controls.negative: E4: frozen bank + Gaussian noise matched to W's token effective rank; expected under the claim: P_N - P_F below 0.5 mean D and P_W - P_N above 0; under the main rival P_N is about P_W
controls.negative_can_move: yes: the noise is added to the tokens the encoder reads, the same place whitening acts
controls.positive: E1: the learned convolution against the frozen bank, the contrast the project record reports
controls.positive_expected: D = P_L - P_F is a signed difference of means with no absolute value, rank or clip, so a known difference comes back unchanged: +109 in the project record (397 vs 288, one seed, 15 patches, GPU); the size at 4 patches and 16,000 steps is unknown, the sign is expected positive

scope.internal: for this tokenizer, bank configuration and training length, how much of the deficit a fixed whitening closes
scope.external: suggests that fixed front ends need a normalisation stage in VQ tokenizers; does not generalise to other bank configurations, longer training, downstream accuracy or other quantizers
limits: one bank configuration (48 poles, 8 oscillators, 4 bins)
16,000 steps with 4 patches per window, not the 44,000 steps and 15 patches of the project record
the because clause is tested only against noise-driven rank inflation; other consequences of whitening are not separated

power.min_detectable: d >= 1.11 at 80% power, one-sided alpha = 0.05 (paired, normal approximation)

claims.statement: The deficit in codebook perplexity of the frozen filter-bank front end against the learned convolution, D = P_L - P_F, is estimated over 5 seeds at this scale with its 95% confidence interval.
reasons: The project record has one seed per arm.

evidence.measure: P per run as in E2 -> per seed D = P_L - P_F -> mean and 95% CI over 5 seeds
evidence.would_show: the size and spread of the deficit

claims.warrant: When the same contrast is run from several seeds, then the mean difference and its interval describe the contrast better than one run.

outcomes.if_supported: a deficit with an interval that excludes zero makes the project's single-seed observation a replicated fact
outcomes.if_not: an interval that includes zero says the deficit is within seed noise at this scale

claims.estimate_because: size-open: the direction is the project record's single-seed observation (397 vs 288); its size and seed-to-seed spread at this scale are unknown
claims.precision_target: 95% CI of total width 1.75 SD of the per-seed difference with n = 5 (SD unknown); aim: an interval that separates the deficit from zero

claims.statement: For the four front-end arms the anisotropy of the tokens (effective rank, signal-subspace rank, mean pairwise cosine) and the effective rank of the quantizer input are reported beside each arm's codebook perplexity.
reasons: The project record found that no offline token statistic predicted the deficit.

evidence.measure: token statistics on 8,800 held-out patches per arm; effective rank of z at step 16,000 per run -> mean per arm; listed with mean perplexity
evidence.would_show: which statistic orders the arms as perplexity does

claims.warrant: When several candidate statistics are listed beside an outcome over the same arms, then the ones that order the arms differently from the outcome are poor predictors of it.

outcomes.if_supported: a statistic that orders the arms as perplexity does becomes a candidate offline screen for front ends
outcomes.if_not: no offline statistic orders them, as the project record found, and the screen has to be a training run

claims.estimate_because: descriptive: four arms give an ordering, not a test
claims.precision_target: per-arm means over 5 (L, F, W) or 3 (N) seeds with their ranges; no interval aimed for

sample.target: EEG tokenizers trained on multi-corpus EEG
sample.accessible: one tokenizer architecture on 55 h of sleep EEG, 5 seeds, plus EEGBCI
sample.concern: small corpus and short training; the project's preprocessing left quality defects in the sleep pool

predictor.phenomenon: the second-order geometry of what the front end hands to the encoder
predictor.validity: construct: whitening changes only mean and covariance of the tokens (manipulation check E0)

outcome.phenomenon: how much of the codebook the tokenizer uses
outcome.precision: between-seed spread unknown; estimated in E1
outcome.accuracy: exact for the EMA usage the quantizer keeps
outcome.validity: content: the usage entropy the VQ literature reports (fangetal2025, takida2022); it is not a measure of downstream usefulness

tradeoffs.change: a centring-only arm (mean removal without variance flattening) was not included
tradeoffs.lost: the split of the whitening effect into its mean-removal part and its variance-flattening part
tradeoffs.why: the question asks about whitening as a whole against training

tradeoffs.change: other bank configurations (12 poles, 26 oscillators) were not included
tradeoffs.because: budget: each configuration needs its own F and W runs
tradeoffs.lost: whether the result holds for less anisotropic banks
tradeoffs.why: the question is asked of the configuration whose deficit is documented; the limit is stated in scope
